ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, authorized representatives, and every ultimate beneficial owner against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, US OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, Egyptian National Terrorist List under Law No. 94 of 2015, and Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT blacklists. Enhanced due diligence is compulsory for any person identified as a Politically Exposed Person, including senior public officials, their family members, and close associates. Continuous transaction and party screening is required post-incorporation, and any PEP or sanctions match must be escalated to senior management and the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit as required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) E-Services Portal and the Commercial Registry of the Egyptian Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered name of an Egyptian Limited Liability Company must be in Arabic script. A transliterated English name may be entered in the auxiliary register but does not replace the Arabic statutory name. The name must include the corporate legal form indication, usually 'LLC' or the Arabic abbreviation reflecting 'Limited Liability Company'. Foreign-language denominations that are not phonetically transliterated into Arabic will generally not be accepted on the formal trade certificate.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Property Investment or any terms implying licensed financial activity without relevant regulator approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If GAFI or the Commercial Registry rejects the proposed company name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with GAFI’s Investor Services and Complaints Unit within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice, attaching the original rejection decision and any evidence of trademark registration, goodwill, or government approval if the name contains a sensitive token. If GAFI upholds the rejection, the applicant may bring an annulment action before the Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council within 60 days of the final administrative decision. A completely new name may be re-filed immediately; the reserved name cannot be extended beyond the initial 30-day reservation window unless an administrative stay or litigation order provides otherwise.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A purely virtual office without any physical presence in Egypt is not compliant for an Egyptian LLC. The company must maintain a fixed registered address within the governorate, with file storage capacity for statutory records and a location that is accessible to tax, labor, and commercial registry inspectors. Serviced offices and co-working physical suites are otherwise acceptable, provided the LLC lease agreement covers dedicated work space and acceptance of official correspondence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 12% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months after incorporation, reflecting the medium-risk rating of automated dropshipping and the Egyptian Commercial Registry and GAFI practice of random compliance visits.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended, principally Articles 59-76 governing limited liability companies, together with its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982, as amended. Foreign investment procedures may also be subject to Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), Companies Establishment Sector, acting through the Companies Registry and the GAFI electronic incorporation portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association, submitted for authentication and registration with GAFI, followed by issuance of the commercial registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Egyptian law does not prescribe a general minimum capital amount for an LLC. The capital and quota allocation must be stated in the incorporation contract, and the subscribed capital must be fully paid at incorporation. No general escrow account is required solely for LLC formation; any sector-specific, foreign-exchange, banking, or investment requirements must be confirmed with GAFI and the receiving bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept and ratify the subscription by each founding quota holder for the quotas allocated in the authenticated Incorporation Contract and confirm that the subscribed capital has been fully paid. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Company adopt its registered office at the address stated in the Incorporation Contract and authorize the Managing Director to execute the lease and related filings. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed Managing Director and [Name] be appointed authorized signatory, each within the powers recorded in the Incorporation Contract and applicable Egyptian law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm permitted activity, ownership, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Establishment Sector and the GAFI electronic incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that online retail and automated dropshipping are permissible activities for an Egyptian LLC and identify any product-specific import, consumer protection, payment, or sector restrictions. Secure a registered-office lease or ownership document and obtain landlord consent where required. If foreign documents are used, legalize them through the issuing state, authenticate them through the Egyptian diplomatic mission, and provide certified Arabic translations.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business purpose
Founders' passports or Egyptian national identity cards
Foreign corporate shareholder documents, if applicable
Powers of attorney, where representatives act for founders
Landlord identification and authorization, where requested
Certified Arabic translations and legalization evidence for foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to GAFI comments through the portal, correct the business purpose or documentary defect, replace a non-compliant office document, and resubmit within the stated cure period. Obtain written clarification from GAFI where the activity classification is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the company name and prepare incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI electronic incorporation portal or GAFI Companies Establishment Sector service counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name, activity description, capital, quota allocation, management structure, registered office, and duration. Prepare the Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association in the prescribed Arabic form. Ensure consistency among names, ownership percentages, powers of the manager, foreign-investor data, and the registered office.
required_dossiers: Draft Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association
Special approvals, if the selected activity or product requires them
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the proposed name or activity wording if rejected, upload corrected documents, and request a renewed electronic review. Escalate unresolved classification issues to the GAFI Companies Establishment Sector.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Authenticate and sign the incorporation contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI authentication and incorporation services, with competent notarial authentication where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange signature by all founders or duly authorized attorneys. Authenticate powers of attorney and foreign corporate resolutions as required. Pay the applicable GAFI, authentication, publication, syndicate, and service charges shown in the official application. Preserve the executed Arabic contract and certified translations.
required_dossiers: Final Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association
Corporate shareholder board or shareholder resolutions
Proof of legal existence and authority of corporate shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct signature, authentication, translation, or authority defects identified by GAFI or the notary. Re-execute defective pages and submit a formal clarification or amended contract before the application expires.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the establishment certificate and commercial registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Establishment Sector and the Commercial Registry Office affiliated with the Internal Trade Development Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authenticated incorporation file and obtain GAFI's establishment certificate. Complete registration in the competent Commercial Registry, verify the registered address and activities, and obtain the commercial registration extract or certificate. Confirm that the manager's authority and company name are recorded accurately.
required_dossiers: Authenticated Incorporation Contract and Articles of Association
Power of attorney for the filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File corrected registry data or an amendment through GAFI and the competent Commercial Registry. Request rectification of clerical errors and retain the registry rejection or query notice for the appeal or resubmission record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, employer, banking, and beneficial-owner onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority, National Social Insurance Authority, commercial bank, and GAFI or other competent beneficial-ownership filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the tax registration certificate and tax identification number, register for VAT if statutory thresholds or taxable activities require it, and register employees with social insurance before employment begins. Open the company bank account, fund the declared capital, and complete bank KYC, AML, foreign-exchange, and beneficial-owner checks. Obtain an electronic tax services account where required.
required_dossiers: Employment and payroll information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer tax, bank, or social-insurance queries with corrected ownership, address, activity, and identification evidence. File amended tax or registry data where discrepancies arise and obtain written confirmation of the cure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) for any future industrial or manufacturing premises; GAFI and the competent Commercial Registry remain the principal authorities for this non-manufacturing online retail activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating or manufacturing permit is ordinarily required for an LLC conducting automated dropshipping and online retail without manufacturing, warehousing subject to special regulation, or a physical industrial facility. Ordinary commercial, tax, consumer-protection, product, import, and premises requirements remain applicable as facts require.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from a project-specific EIA for a purely digital dropshipping business with no manufacturing, material storage, emissions, wastewater discharge, or regulated waste facility. A screening or environmental approval may become necessary if the business establishes a warehouse, fulfillment center, packaging operation, or other physical facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, industrial emissions, VOC discharge, or hazardous-waste generation should be created by the stated model. Any future facility must comply with Environmental Law No. 4 of 1994, as amended, its Executive Regulations, applicable EEAA approvals, wastewater discharge limits, air-emission and VOC controls, hazardous-waste segregation and licensed disposal rules, and municipal requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defense or occupational clearance is ordinarily required for a purely virtual office with no employees or physical operations. Any office, warehouse, fulfillment center, or packaging premises must obtain applicable local occupancy and fire-safety approvals from the Civil Protection authority, satisfy building and structural-load requirements, maintain emergency exits and fire systems, and complete workplace health and safety registrations or inspections required by the competent labor and local authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) under the Ministry of Finance – integrated digital portal: www.eta.gov.eg; e-invoicing platform via eta.gov.eg/einvoice; customs data exchanged through the Nafeza single-window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and register in the Commercial Registry. Step 2: File tax card (TIN) application with ETA within 30 days of commercial registration; LLC obtains a single Tax Identification Number (TIN) covering income tax, VAT, and payroll. Step 3: Mandatory VAT registration once annual taxable supplies reach EGP 500,000 or immediately for non-resident e-commerce suppliers. Step 4: Obtain ETA digital credentials and activate e-invoice/e-receipt profiles; a licensed Egyptian tax agent is permitted to act for non-resident principals. A foreign-owned Egyptian LLC is fully eligible to hold a TIN without additional state approval.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Egyptian LLC is a per-se corporate taxpayer under Law 91/2005 (taxable on worldwide income at 22.5% CIT) and Law 67/2016 (VAT). No pass-through treatment is available to LLC members; profits distributed to non-resident shareholders attract 10% dividend withholding (treaty-reduced to 5%–15% where applicable). Goods and designated services physically exported are zero-rated and removed from the taxable base (territorial export carve-out).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists; LLC classification is statutory and immutable. Relevant elections: (i) GAFI Free Zone / Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) election granting VAT and CIT exemptions on qualifying export activities; (ii) ETA-approved off-calendar fiscal year election; (iii) exporter refund election for rapid input VAT refund via the ETA settlement mechanism; (iv) advance pricing agreement (APA) election for cross-border related-party transactions; (v) investment incentive election under Investment Law 72/2017 for new capital-intensive projects.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, with separate excise regime (Law 67 also covering selective tax schedules).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable supplies (mandatory registration threshold per VAT Law 67/2016 Art. 34); voluntary registration from EGP 100,000; automated dropshipping enterprises must monitor disaggregated cross-platform turnover to avoid threshold breach.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing (B2B/B2G) and e-receipts (B2C) for all VAT-registered taxpayers per ETA phase-in decisions (Decision No. 641/2022 and subsequent phases). Invoices must be transmitted in real time via the ETA Portal REST-API (JSON/XML, EDIFACT-compatible) or the web UI; ETA validates each document and returns a unique UUID plus QR digital stamp. Fiscal clearance is centralized: unmatched or non-compliant invoices invalidate input VAT credit and block issue of Tax Clearance Certificates (TCC). Cross-border export invoices are integrated with the Nafeza customs declaration system for verification of physical exit.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: VAT zero-rating applies when goods are sold to a non-resident and physically exported from Egypt under a valid customs declaration (including dropshipped goods warehoused in and shipped from Egypt). Services: automated intermediation, platform, and support fees qualify as zero-rated export of services when supplied to a non-resident recipient, not effectively consumed in Egypt, and supported by written contracts and payment evidence. Conversely, if goods are fulfilled directly from offshore warehouses with only routing and payment processing in Egypt, the service fee may qualify for zero-rating while the underlying goods sale falls outside Egyptian VAT scope; the LLC must maintain complete supply-chain mapping to prove the distinction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Nafeza/ETA digital export declaration)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure
Inward Remittance Certificate from an Egyptian authorized bank
Export commercial invoice and sales agreement
Foreign currency conversion/transfer report confirming repatriation
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA and Central Bank of Egypt cross-match export declarations, e-invoice data, and banking FX records; refunds are suspended automatically if repatriation exceeds 180 days. Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger retrospective clawback of refunded VAT plus late-payment surcharge of 2% per month (capped at 100%), fines of up to 300% of the evaded tax, criminal imprisonment up to 5 years, disgorgement of CIT deductions and free-zone benefits, TCC denial, and de-registration under Law 67/2016 Arts. 31–40 and Tax Procedure Law 67/2016.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting under Law No. 88 of 2003 and the Foreign Exchange Instructions; the CBE is the sole licensing, supervision, and exchange-control authority for all inward and outward capital flows, treasury operations, and payment clearing. The General Authority for Investment (GAFI) administers investment registration while the CBE controls all FX execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has operated a unified, market-determined exchange-rate regime since March 2024, so both current and capital transactions are technically convertible through authorized banks. However, the CBE retains discretionary monitoring and banks must independently validate the underlying commercial transaction before executing any FX operation. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation require completion of a licensed-bank source-of-funds review, audited financial statements, a valid tax clearance certificate, and evidence that the original share capital was brought into Egypt through a licensed bank. E-wallet and digital-payment settlement accounts may be used only as collecting channels and must be periodically swept into a domestic CBE-licensed account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the CBE Export Proceeds Instructions, export receipts must be repatriated to Egypt through an authorized bank within 30 days of the agreed payment date stated in the underlying export contract. Following the March 2024 liberalization, there is no mandatory fixed percentage of export proceeds that must be converted into Egyptian pounds; exporters may retain 100% of the proceeds in a foreign-currency account with the receiving licensed bank. Each inbound payment must still be matched against the relevant export invoice and reported to the CBE on the prescribed reporting forms to support future import payments or profit remittances.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EGP and USD) and Import/Export Foreign-Currency Account
Operational Account and Share Capital Escrow Account for LLC establishment
Operational Account and Capital Deposit Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: QNB Al Ahli (Qatar National Bank Egypt)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Trade-Finance Foreign-Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Egypt does not issue corporate settlement licenses to foreign digital banks, electronic-money institutions, or offshore virtual-account providers. Stripe and PayPal are acceptable solely as e-commerce acquiring and collection rails; the aggregated proceeds must be withdrawn through SWIFT to a bank account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank. Any attempt to clear ultimate corporate liquidity through Wise, Payoneer, or a similar unlicensed EMI will trigger AML rejection and potential de-risking by the local correspondent bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for corporate account onboarding. The General Manager, all authorized signatories, and each beneficial owner must attend the bank's branch in person to complete the customer due-diligence interview and exhibit original identification and corporate documents. Remote opening through video calls or online portals is not accepted for a non-resident-controlled LLC; certified copies of passports, apostilled/consular-legalized constituent documents, and GAFI registration certificates are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly incorporated dropshipping LLC presents immediately with high-volume, low-value card or e-wallet receipts from Stripe and PayPal without a tangible commercial footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform RMS and consolidated transaction history from Stripe and PayPal; customer order logs with IP/adress linkage; fulfillment and tracking documentation; supplier invoices and purchase orders; logistics contracts and customs entry declarations; a board-approved business narrative describing the automated order-brokering model; and monthly data-reconciliation methodology between gateway settlements and bank deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership mismatch or opacity among the non-resident ultimate shareholder, the Egyptian manager, and the payment-rail signatory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Incorporation and constitutional documents with a complete UBO schedule; notarized board resolution appointing a single Banking Authorized Signatory; certified passport copies of all shareholders; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letters from the investor's home bank; proof of commercial address; GAFI registration certificate with shareholding schedule under Law No. 72 of 2017; and tax card issued by the Egyptian Tax Authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid e-commerce cash velocity raises suspicion of layering, invoice-consolidation fraud, or unauthorized settlement of regulated automobile-related payments through an unlicensed retail pass-through.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A SKU-level product catalog with cross-references to ISIC 4791; supplier sale agreements with HS codes; warranty and returns documentation; daily transaction-log reconciliation between gateway reports and the LLC's revenue accounting system; clearance certificates from the payment networks confirming no money-laundering or sanctions flags; and a bank-validated compliance program reflecting transaction monitoring thresholds suitable for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced dropshipping entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must arrive via SWIFT MT103 using the CBE-reporting purpose code for direct investment into the establishment capital of an Egyptian legal entity. The LLC must first open a non-resident share-capital escrow account at the selected licensed bank, receive the USD or EUR transfer against the beneficial-owner source-of-funds file, and, after GAFI registration and CBE acknowledgment, convert the funds into EGP at the prevailing interbank bid rate. For each incoming wire the bank executes CBE Form ETP reporting, verifies the remitter's identity, and logs the inward-transfer voucher which will later be used to support profit remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier settlements are executed through SWIFT MT103 for open-account or advance-payment arrangements and through irrevocable sight Letters of Credit or documentary collections where supplier credit discipline is preferred. Every disbursement requires a signed supplier pro-forma invoice, the original purchase order, and the CBE import-payment documentation. Dropshipping receipts aggregated from Stripe and PayPal are cleared against disbursements by presenting the gateway settlement statements, the corresponding supplier invoice, and the logistics proof presented to the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright EGP/USD forwards with a trade-flow underlying and tenor not exceeding 12 months
Back-to-back FX swaps and matched currency swaps executed through CBE-authorized banks at interbank prices
FX forwards and swaps combined with Import/Export Letters of Credit to lock the local-currency cost of dropshipping inventory
Offshore non-deliverable forwards or swaps only where the transaction is genuinely trade-related, settled in a foreign currency outside Egypt, and never settled in EGP domestically

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and self-assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the tax year; calendar-year LLCs must file by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 2% per month or part-month on unpaid corporate tax, capped at 100% of the tax; ETA best-judgment assessment; interest accrual on delayed payments; enforced collection against bank accounts and company assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and auditor's report approved by the annual ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); copy attached to ETA tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end; calendar-year LLCs must complete approval by 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may become personally liable for deficits caused by failure to approve accounts; GAFI may issue corrective orders for repeated non-compliance and ultimately petition for compulsory winding-up; dividend distributions are suspended until financial statements are approved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office under the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade, coordinated through GAFI one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for calendar-year companies; alternate fiscal-year companies renew within 3 months of the anniversary of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal surcharges are imposed progressively; suspension of the commercial registration occurs after repeated non-renewal; continued failure for 12 months or more may lead to administrative strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GAFI annual company file renewal fee and declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the first quarter of the calendar year or within 30 days after the registration anniversary for newly incorporated LLCs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty interest applied at 2% per month; GAFI suspends corporate services, certificate issuance, and amendment approvals; non-payment for 6 months can trigger administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and update of shareholders register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EFIU) and Commercial Registry through GAFI
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership and in every annual Commercial Registry renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False, incomplete, or late beneficial ownership data exposes responsible officers to administrative fines and criminal sanctions under AML Law 80/2002 as amended; the Commercial Registry may refuse renewal until corrected; repeated violations invite strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual payroll withholding tax and salary reconciliation return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the close of the tax year; calendar-year LLCs generally file by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 2% per month on net withholding differences, interest for late payment, disallowance of employee cost deductions, and personal liability of directors for unremitted employee tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit is compulsory for an Egyptian LLC when issued capital exceeds EGP 250,000, when a shareholder or creditor lawfully requests an audit, or when the ETA requires audited accounts due to turnover or risk classification. Small dropshipping LLCs below these thresholds may file unaudited accounts but must still maintain complete accounting records.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), closely aligned with IFRS as adopted by the Egyptian Ministry of Finance; statutory financial statements must be prepared in Egyptian pounds unless an alternative currency is approved by the ETA.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egyptian AML/CFT requirements oblige every LLC to identify and verify all ultimate beneficial owners, being natural persons owning 25% or more of capital or voting rights, or exercising control by other means. The LLC must maintain a current beneficial ownership register and reconfirm the data during the annual Commercial Registry renewal; material changes must be filed within 30 days. There is no separate government fee for the UBO confirmation itself, but false declarations carry administrative and criminal liability.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800–2,200 per year for a small automated dropshipping LLC without subsidiaries

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% (standard CIT rate under Law No. 91 of 2005; a temporary 1.5% solidarity addition under Law No. 26 of 2020 has expired, restoring the headline rate to 22.5% for current tax periods).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME presumptive regime under Law No. 152 of 2020: eligible small and medium companies with annual turnover up to EGP 50 million may elect tax on gross revenue at 0.5% (<= EGP 2m turnover), 1.5% (EGP 2m-10m) or 3% (EGP 10m-50m) in lieu of the 22.5% CIT. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017: deduction of up to 50% (priority/underdeveloped regions) or 30% (other regions) of capital investment costs from taxable profit for new/expansion projects. Public free zones: qualifying export-oriented profits may be wholly CIT-exempt. Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) and classified investment-zone projects may access preferential CIT treatment. Qualifying Egyptian-resident corporate shareholders enjoy a participation exemption for dividend income. Interest deductibility is subject to EBITDA-based limitation and thin-cap rules under Law No. 26 of 2020 (BEPS 4 implementation).
